ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on $AB$, $OD$ bisects $\angle BOC$, $\angle 1=20^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\because \angle 1=20^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOC=180^\circ-\angle 1=180^\circ-20^\circ=160^\circ$,\\
$\because$ OD bisects $\angle BOC$,\\
$\therefore \angle 2=\boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, A, O, and B are located on the same horizontal straight line, with O in the middle; ray OC is drawn from O toward the upper left, and ray OD is drawn from O toward the upper right. Angle 1 is marked between OA and OC, and angle 2 is marked between OD and OB. Then reason: It is known that ∠1 = 20°, and OD bisects ∠BOC. Let ∠2 = x, then because OD bisects ∠BOC, ∠COD = x. A, O, and B are collinear, so from OA through OC and OD to OB forms a straight angle of 180°, so 20° + x + x = 180°. Solving gives 2x = 160°, x = 80°. Therefore ∠2 = 80°.

method.method_draft: From the image, read that A, O, B lie on one straight horizontal line, ray OC goes upward-left, ray OD goes upward-right, angle 1 is the angle between OA and OC, and angle 2 is the angle between OD and OB. From the text, use that angle 1 is 20° and OD bisects angle BOC. Let angle 2 be x. Since OD bisects angle BOC, angle COD also equals x. The straight angle from OA through OC, OD, to OB is 180°, so 20° + x + x = 180°. Solve x = 80°, so angle 2 is 80°.
